subject: Adoption of Twenty-Four Precinct Redistricting Plan
overview: The Council adopted a new redistricting map that increases the city's precincts to 24 to manage future population growth and referred a major zoning ordinance recodification to the Community Development Board. The body also established a working group to address rodent infestations and discussed expanding senior tax deferment eligibility.

items.title: Clear Channel Billboard Relocation and Upgrade
items.summary: Approved the relocation and digital upgrade of a billboard at 236-240 Mystic Avenue, which includes a $25,000 annual linkage fee and public service messaging allotments.

items.title: Zoning Ordinance Recodification Public Hearing
items.summary: Referred the citywide zoning ordinance recodification to the Community Development Board to allow for additional stakeholder input on the 100-page working document.

items.title: City Infrastructure and Maintenance
items.summary: Approved requests for a five-year paving report, the marking of exposed castings on Mystic Avenue, repair of a High Street pothole, and installation of crosswalks at Salem Street intersections.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Condolences
items.summary: Approved resolutions recognizing 2021 Boston Marathon participants, celebrating the 50th wedding anniversary of Michael and Marie Price, and offering condolences for several residents and a retired firefighter.

items.title: Resident Notification of 5G Facilities
items.summary: Approved a resolution requiring the city administration to notify residents via reverse 911 calls regarding the locations of 17 approved 5G small cell towers.

items.title: Regional Rodent Control Working Group
items.summary: Approved the creation of a professional working group to address rodent infestations, with amendments to include surrounding communities and develop a liability waiver for treating private property.

items.title: Redistricting Map Adoption
items.summary: Adopted Plan C for reprecincting in a 4-3 vote, which increases the number of city precincts from 16 to 24 to accommodate projected population growth over the next decade.

items.title: Senior Tax Deferment Income Limits
items.summary: Referred a proposal to tie the income limit for senior tax deferments to the state circuit breaker tax credit cap to the Committee of the Whole for further legal and financial review.

items.title: School Area Construction and Air Quality
items.summary: Approved resolutions to restrict construction hours near the Brooks School to follow student drop-off and requested standards for air quality testing in all public buildings.

items.title: Staffing Updates and Organizational Chart
items.summary: Requested comprehensive updates on City Hall staffing vacancies, a named organizational chart, the Fire Department leadership transition, and Medford Community Media hiring.

items.title: Public Participation: National Grid Repairs
items.summary: Resident Nate Merritt criticized the noise levels, lack of notification, and extended duration of a National Grid gas leak repair project at the intersection of Riverside Avenue and Locust Street.
